solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: An innocent artist captures hearts in palace

parts.note: the article gives the letter A

indicators.note: the artist's phrase captures, i.e. holds within it, the next piece

parts.note: a lamb is the stock image of an innocent
H is the card-suit abbreviation for hearts
RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A naive painter sketches a palace with hearts woven into the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alhambra is the Moorish palace-fortress in Granada, Spain.

clue.text: Sheltered side at church for scrounger

parts.note: the lee is the side sheltered from the wind

explanation.surface: Someone loiters on the sheltered side of a church, sponging off worshippers.
explanation.definitionFit: A leech is a parasite, figuratively a person who sponges off others.

clue.text: Last in race hated U. Bolt moving quickly

indicators.note: letters that are moving are being shifted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
U is taken as written, the initial standing for itself
taken as written

indicators.note: the final letter of the word race is taken

explanation.surface: Usain Bolt, finishing last in a race he hated, is pictured hurrying along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' looks like part of the definition 'moving quickly', but it is the anagram signal: E (from 'Last in race') plus HATED, U and BOLT are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The military idiom for running or hurrying, so it means quickly or at once.

clue.text: Frenzied Schubert kills cruelly

indicators.note: something frenzied is wildly agitated, so the composer's letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A crazed Schubert goes on a murderous rampage.
explanation.definitionFit: To butcher is to slaughter savagely, a verb meaning kill brutally.

clue.text: Thus saw deal as hostile to principles?

definitions.meaning: deal is pine timber; sawing it across its fibres is one way to cut it
idiom for going contrary to one's natural inclinations or beliefs

explanation.surface: A carpenter's cutting method doubles as a phrase for opposing one's principles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal' is not a bargain but softwood planking, a sense less known outside Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a literal woodworking direction across fibres and an idiom for running contrary to one's nature.

clue.text: Minor insult

definitions.meaning: small or trivial, as an adjective
a snub or affront, as a noun

explanation.definitionFit: The word works as an adjective meaning small and as a noun meaning a snub.

clue.text: Letter from Greeks about Turkish leader brings disgrace

indicators.note: the Greek letter goes about, around, the next piece

parts.note: sigma is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: the leader of Turkish is its first letter

explanation.surface: A letter sent by Greece about the Turkish president causes diplomatic shame.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of shame, a synonym for disgrace.

clue.text: Princess thought Spain expendable

indicators.note: the Spain letter is expendable, so it can be dropped from the thought

parts.note: an idea is a thought
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A royal considered Spain something she could do without.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Ida is the title character of a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Ida is the princess of Gilbert and Sullivan's opera and Tennyson's poem The Princess.

clue.text: Devil's burner for wealthy fellow gone mad

indicators.note: mad letters are crazed, so the remaining letters are jumbled
with the fellow letter gone, it is removed from the first word

explanation.surface: A rich man who has lost his mind is likened to a fiery demon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone' takes F from FOR, leaving OR, which is then rearranged with WEALTHY under 'mad'.
explanation.definitionFit: Folklore says blessed water scalds demons, so it is aptly called what burns the Devil.

clue.text: St Peter not entirely muddled in group

indicators.note: muddled letters are mixed up and reordered
not entirely means the final letter of the saint's name is dropped

explanation.surface: The apostle, a little confused, finds himself in a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' cuts STPETER to STPETE, which 'muddled' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A septet is a group of seven, especially of musicians.

clue.text: Friendly before noon, I wired message

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means before noon
a cable is a telegram sent by wire

explanation.surface: Someone sent a warm telegram one morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable means friendly and goodwilled, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Ring that woman keeps as last product

indicators.note: the pronoun keeps, holds within it, the round letter

parts.note: she is the pronoun for that woman
a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A woman holds on to a ring as her final creation.
explanation.walkthrough: A last is a cobbler's foot-shaped mould, so 'last' is not 'final' here.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwear is shaped over a cobbler's last, so it is what that form produces.

clue.text: Give Neo blue garment bequeathed

parts.note: to hand is to give
the setter Neo refers to themself, so Neo gives me
down means blue, sad

explanation.surface: The setter asks for a sad piece of clothing left in a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-me-down is a used garment passed on to someone, as if inherited.

clue.text: Hydrated or not, ultimately unwell, in need of water

indicators.note: unwell letters are out of sorts, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of the word not

explanation.surface: Whether hydrated or not, a sick patient is crying out for water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' looks like part of 'Hydrated or not', but only its last letter T is used; 'unwell' rearranges HYDRATED, OR and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Being parched in the throat means being thirsty, wanting a drink.

clue.text: Populist met with Draco in dispute

indicators.note: letters in dispute are in disarray, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man of the people argued with the harsh Athenian lawgiver Draco.
explanation.definitionFit: A democrat champions rule by the common people, so is a populist.

clue.text: Among Europeans Tory order is seen to make cuts

indicators.note: the following pieces are placed among, between, the two European letters

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European, so two Europeans give two Es
CON is short for Conservative, the Tory party
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A Conservative instruction across Europe is to slash spending.
explanation.walkthrough: The OM (Order of Merit) is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: To economise is to reduce spending, i.e. make cuts.

clue.text: At this time one becomes legendary creature

parts.note: yet means up to this time
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Right now a single being turns into a myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeti is the abominable snowman of Himalayan legend.

clue.text: Apostle takes position on women

parts.note: a stand is a position taken
re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: A disciple takes a stance on women's issues.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Andrew was one of the twelve apostles of Jesus.

clue.text: Marsupial dropping by deep dark centre

indicators.note: the marsupial is dropping, losing, the letters for by

parts.note: a wombat is an Australian marsupial
at can mean by, as in at the door

explanation.surface: Wombat droppings lie beside a deep, dark hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: The uterus is poetically a deep, dark, central hollow where life begins.

clue.text: Thearchy at sea in 18 of trout

definitions.note: 18 across refers to a womb, so this is where trout are bred

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A divine government adrift in the womb of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish farm where eggs are incubated is the breeding place, figuratively the womb, of trout.

clue.text: Golden Penny kept by the Aussie Pools winner

indicators.note: the gold and penny pieces are kept by, held within, the word the

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: An Australian football pools winner pockets a golden penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pools' looks like the British football pools betting game, but it means swimming pools.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian Thorpe was an Australian swimmer who won Olympic gold medals in the pool.

clue.text: Free hotel in secure enclosure close to Asian capital

indicators.note: the free and hotel pieces go in the enclosure

parts.note: a cage is a secure enclosure
open means free, unrestricted
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the close, last letter, of Asian is taken

explanation.surface: A free hotel stands inside a guarded compound near an Asian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Asian capital' looks like the definition, but only N (close to Asian) is used; the capital is European.
explanation.definitionFit: Copenhagen is the capital city of Denmark.

clue.text: No surgical procedures? I've made a mistake!

parts.note: O can stand for nothing, zero
ops is short for operations

explanation.surface: A surgeon admits an error after there are no operations.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation uttered on making a blunder.

clue.text: See 25
Six agents circling hill station

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: the agents are circling, surrounding, the hill

parts.note: CIA is the American intelligence agency
a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: Six spies surround a hill station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hill station' looks like the definition; Victoria is a major London railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: London Victoria is a major railway station.

clue.text: Leaves much to be desired at this gathering!

definitions.text: Leaves much to be desired at this gathering!

parts.words: Leaves much to be desired at this gathering!
parts.note: the leaves are ... leaves for brewing, much wanted at a social afternoon event

explanation.definitionFit: An afternoon social gathering where a drink brewed from leaves is served.

clue.text: Delay where Ginger embraces sailor

indicators.note: the red colour embraces, holds, the sailor

parts.note: ginger hair is red
tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A red-headed person hugs a sailor and holds him back.
explanation.definitionFit: To retard is to slow down or hold back, so to delay.

clue.text: Be sent back in time for discussion

indicators.note: the reversed word sits in the time

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: sent back means the word be is reversed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Being sent back in time to talk things over.
explanation.definitionFit: A debate is a formal discussion of opposing views.

clue.text: Impossible situation for lawyer, old Bob, in present times

indicators.note: the phrase meaning impossible is the situation, the setting, for the lawyer

parts.note: no way means impossible
DA is a district attorney
a bob was a shilling in old British money, abbreviated S

explanation.surface: A lawyer and an old man called Bob face an impossible situation today.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob was a pre-decimal British shilling, abbreviated s.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowadays means in these present times, at the present day.
